newsitem.title: FINLAND: NESTE SAYS GAZPROM DEAL PRELIMINARY.
newsitem.headline: NESTE SAYS GAZPROM DEAL PRELIMINARY.

text.p: An agreement on Friday between Finnish energy group Neste and Russia's RAO Gazprom on a joint venture to implement a European natural gas pipeline project is preliminary and means looking at feasibility, Neste said.
Aili Kytokivi, spokeswoman for Neste's natural gas arm Gasum Oy, said no details were yet clear except that the heads of both companies had decided on the preliminary deal.
"It's at the feasibility stage. This is now to connect Russia's natural gas reserves via Finland to central Europe," she said.
No details either about the potential capacity for the pipeline or the venture's capital structure were yet available, she said.

The deal followed a similar one late last year when Neste said the European Union's Council of Ministers had agreed to include another project, involving other Nordic gas and energy companies, in its list of Trans-European Energy Networks (TEN).
It said then a first feasibility study would explore alternatives to link the Nordic natural gas networks.
Kytokivi said Friday's deal would look at the central European market. "Of course we will try to find out what connection the two (projects) could have," she added.
Neste said in its statement the two companies aimed to implement the project by 2005.
